chapter_note: Chapter contains a robust substrate teaching about the Sun: a seven-good enumeration (with parallel seven-evils of night), then a five-fold mapping (light/beauty/peace/life/power), then three mysteries linking sun to the First Greatness/Father. The substrate is wrapped in a heavy editorial frame: opening dialogue setup, anti-Zoroastrian/anti-Errant polemic (i=9-20, i=56-60, i=138-139) about those who refuse to recognize the Sun, citation of the Savior (i=140-142), citation of Pauline 'sons of light' formula (i=143-145), and a final hortatory address to 'my beloved'. Editorial fatigue drift toward later layers in second half is partially explained by the polemic+citation+exhortation cluster that closes the chapter. The cosmic-correspondential teaching (sun→Father, hiddenness of disc→hiddenness of Father, exalted height→exalted Father) is genuine substrate cosmological mapping.
